question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,A=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 18 \\ 18 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & 18 \\ 18 & 17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=24+17+18=59.
$$
